articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Latest Developments in GIS' (Digest No.41)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: The conditions which could cause breakdown in a GIS are almost always accompanied by partial discharge activity. The discharges may be detected very efficiently by measurements at UHF, and the source of the problem located. The author discusses this type of partial discharge monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: An indoor 420 kV gas insulated substation (GIS) is installed at the Torness 1300 MW AGR Power Station situated on the east coast of Scotland some 50 km from Edinburgh. The Torness 420 kV 50 kA 4000 A GIS installation consists of an 8 circuit-breaker mesh arrangement with two 660 MW generator connected in-feeds, four cable/overhead line circuits, two of which are 'teed' with a shunt reactor and two 420 kV/145 kV interbus transformers connected directly to the GIS busbars via SF/sub 6//oil bushings. The operation of the substation is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evolution of the EHV SF/sub 6/ circuit breaker
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: The author describes the evolution of the SF/sub 6/ EHV circuit breaker from its original six-break per phase to four, two, and one-break versions for both dead-tank GIS and open-terminal designs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: Gas-insulated metalclad substations have a history extending back almost four decades, and SF/sub 6/ has been used for 20 years. The by-products of arcing in SF/sub 6/ can be dealt with satisfactorily by suitably designing the switchgear and the insulating properties of the gas can be maintained throughout the service life of the equipment. The design of a new substation, the GMT11, is described. It has a rated voltage of 145 kV and a rated current of 3150 A.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: The author looks at the CEGB experiences with circuit breakers and substations. Improvements in the performance of circuit breakers associated with GIS substations is discussed. The 400 kV substations are monitored to reduce outages and optimise maintenance procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Latest Developments in GIS
abstract: The high dielectric strength of SF/sub 6/ gas is exploited in a number of applications including gas insulated substations (GIS). It is expensive, however, and there has been an ongoing interest over the years in using mixtures consisting of cheaper buffer gases such as air and nitrogen with added SF/sub 6/ to produce a comparatively cheap mixture with a dielectric strength almost as good as pure SF/sub 6/. The author looks at the effects of additives on the mechanism of breakdown and on point/plane gaps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
